A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotionClone and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v4, including equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices, were readable.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation experiments, automatic metrics and a 20-volunteer study in Table 1, quantitative ablations in Table 2, and qualitative results throughout the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 reports original results on 40 reference videos, automatic metrics and human ratings in Table 1, image/sketch-conditioned generation, qualitative ablations, failure cases, and additional appendix examples.

M1.justification: V1 uses DDIM inversion, time-dependent reference attention, and a sibling-generation branch for location-aware semantic guidance. V4 removes the semantic branch and instead extracts a fixed sparse motion representation through noise addition and one denoising pass, reusing it during generation (Sections 3.3–3.4). It also incorporates SparseCtrl for image/sketch conditioning. The underlying top-k temporal-attention principle remains.

E1.justification: V4 extends reference-motion-guided text-to-video generation to first-frame-conditioned image-to-video and sketch-to-video generation, demonstrated in Section 4.5 and Figure 7. Evaluation also uses DAVIS plus web-sourced videos and introduces explicit subtle-motion and overlapping-object failure scenarios. Both versions retain camera and object motion coverage.

E2.justification: MotionCtrl participates in v1's camera-motion comparison (Figure 6) but disappears from v4's corresponding comparison and baseline list. Dedicated vanilla AnimateDiff comparisons in v1 Figures 5 and 12 also disappear, although uncontrolled examples remain in Figure 2. Both Table 1 comparisons retain VMC, VideoComposer, Gen-1, Tune-A-Video, and Control-A-Video.

E3.justification: The evaluation set changes from 30 DAVIS text-video pairs to 40 DAVIS/web videos, comprising 15 camera-motion and 25 object-motion videos. For real-video references, v1 specifies 500 generation and 300 guidance steps; v4 specifies 100/50 for camera motion and 300/180 for object motion. Guidance changes from two temporal blocks to up_block.1, with revised guidance weights. CLIP metrics and the 20-volunteer, 1–5 rating protocol remain.

E4.justification: V1's quantitative ablations of motion control, threshold masking, and semantic control (Table 2) are removed. V4 adds qualitative studies of sparsity k, extraction timestep, attention block, prompt specificity, and inversion strategy (Figures 3, 8–9), plus illustrated failure cases (Figure 10). The plain-versus-primary attention comparison in Figure 2 is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report average automatic scores and mean ratings from 20 volunteers without generation run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V4 introduces no new statistical uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 scores change throughout. MotionClone's automatic text alignment/temporal consistency are 0.342/0.949 in v1 and 0.3187/0.9621 in v4, while it remains highest in every reported row. These are replacement results under revised methods and evaluation sets, not comparable performance gains or losses. V1's quantitative ablation results disappear, and v4 adds application, sensitivity, failure-case, and revised appendix results.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification changes substantially. V4 Equation 2 replaces direct addition of an energy value with a negative energy gradient scaled by the diffusion noise schedule. V4 also defines the fixed-time sparse representation and associated loss in Equation 6, while removing v1's threshold-mask definition and Gaussian-weighted semantic-guidance formulation. The basic diffusion and temporal-attention definitions remain.

C1.justification: Training-free motion cloning through sparse temporal attention remains the central claim. However, v4 removes location-aware semantic guidance as a principal contribution and foregrounds inversion-free, single-step representation extraction, reuse across denoising steps, and applicability beyond text-to-video. These changes redefine the contribution statements in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: V1 explains spatial implausibility through motion/appearance misalignment and warns about incompatible motion-prompt pairs and structural leakage in Appendix D. V4 replaces this discussion with explanations for fixed-step guidance, timestep sensitivity, and weak dependence on reference prompts. Its limitations attribute subtle-motion failures to low latent resolution and overlapping-object failures to coupled motion (Section 4.7, Figure 10).

D1.justification: V4 provides a substantially revised implementation recipe, specifying SparseCtrl, k=1, extraction timestep 400, null-text reference prompts, and revised guidance settings. V1's explicit 16-frame, 512-by-512 specification and approximate runtime information are omitted. The listed repository changes from Bujiazi/MotionClone to LPengYang/MotionClone, and Appendix A.2 adds directions to example videos; resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V4 adds SparseCtrl, MOFA-Video, and AnyV2V, including discussion of AnyV2V's dense feature injection in Section 2.3. The DDIM reference by Song and colleagues is removed, although inversion remains discussed. Most related-work coverage and positioning are retained; MotionCtrl remains cited despite its removal as an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The former two-component Methodology section becomes separate Motion Representation and Motion Guidance sections. Experiments gain distinct application, analysis, and limitations sections, while Appendices A–E are consolidated into A.1–A.3 with accompanying content changes.

P2.justification: The pipeline diagram is redrawn, the teaser and comparison panels are redesigned, and new representation heatmaps, conditioning demonstrations, sensitivity panels, and failure illustrations appear. V1's Table 2 and dedicated AnimateDiff comparison figures disappear. Appendix galleries are replaced and organized into camera/object examples, alongside extensive changes to typography, captions, headers, and panel arrangements.

improvement.justification: V4 improves technical clarity through the corrected guidance equation and simpler inversion-free formulation, supported by targeted timestep, layer, prompt, and inversion comparisons. Image/sketch demonstrations and illustrated failures better establish applicability. The net gain is limited because the new diagnostic evidence is qualitative, quantitative component ablations are no longer provided, and no updated runtime measurements substantiate the stronger efficiency emphasis. The changed evaluation set also prevents a direct performance-improvement claim.
